title: Continuous rational realization commutes with derived direct image
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site of $T=X,Y$ put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ and $E_T=B_T[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Use the raw rationalization $D^b_c(T,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], with the integral category including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Write $Q_T$ for scalar localization. Let $J_T:D^b_c(T,E)\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(E_T))$ be the continuous rational realization of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], namely $J_T(Q_TK)=E_T\otimes^L_{B_T}K$. Module sheaves and their ambient derived categories are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $Rf_*^B$ denote ordinary ringed-topos derived direct image on $B$-module complexes. On the complete integral subcategory use its canonical identification with the derived strict-tower construction $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{*,n}(K\otimes^L_{B_X}(A/\varpi^n)_X)$ [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Its restriction is bounded constructible, with the integral categories identified by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] and finiteness supplied by [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible]. Let $Rf_*^{\mathrm{rat}}$ be its raw scalar localization [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. Then the canonical localization projection map is an isomorphism
$$E_Y\otimes^L_{B_Y}Rf_*^BK\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*^{E}\bigl(E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K\bigr)$$
for every integral constructible $K$, where $Rf_*^{E}$ is the ordinary right derived direct image of continuous $E_T$-module sheaves. Equivalently, it gives a natural isomorphism
$$J_Y Rf_*^{\mathrm{rat}}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*^{E}J_X.$$
Under the pullback comparison in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], this identifies the completed-pullback/direct-image adjunction on the raw rationalized categories with the restriction of the ambient derived module adjunction; in particular it identifies their actual units and counits. The comparison commutes with finite extensions $E\subset L$, with the canonical coefficient comparisons and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], and with identity maps. It asserts a comparison of the two given direct-image constructions, not an identification with discrete non-torsion coefficients on the small etale site.

proof.text: The separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X$ and $Y$ are noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (the field $k$ is noetherian) and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], and the hypothesis that $\ell$ is invertible supplies the coefficient hypotheses for the completed adic datum. The definitions of $B_T$ and $E_T$, the module categories, and their ambient derived categories are therefore the ones fixed by the cited coefficient and category nodes. The realization functor is the specified $J_T(Q_TK)=E_T\otimes^L_{B_T}K$.

source.place: Propositions 6.6.11 and 6.8.14(2), with the coefficient and ambient-category definitions

proof.text: For an integral constructible $K$, the direct image used in the statement is the ordinary ringed-topos derived direct image on $B$-modules, and its restriction to the complete integral category is the strict tower $R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{*,n}(K\otimes^L_{B_X}(A/\varpi^n)_X)$. The identification of the ordinary derived direct image with this tower, its reduction maps, and derived completeness are exactly the conclusions of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] together with the definition [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

The output $Rf_*^BK$ is again in the integral bounded constructible category: the stratified-perfect characterization identifies that category with the completed integral objects, while the finite-type integral direct-image theorem gives constructibility of every reduction, a uniform cohomological bound, and the canonical reduction isomorphisms. The hypotheses needed there hold because $f$ is a morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes and $\ell$ is invertible in $k$.

The finiteness needed for localization is qcqs. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X$ is noetherian (the field $k$ is noetherian). For both $f$ and its diagonal $\Delta_f$, the inverse image of an affine open of the target is an open subset of the noetherian space $X$, hence quasi-compact. Thus $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Here quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. These are precisely the geometric hypotheses in [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image], which will be applied to the sequence of complexes with transition $\varpi$.

source.place: Geometric hypotheses for bounded continuity; elementary qcqs verification

proof.text: Write $S_T=E_T$ and $C_T=S_T\otimes^L_{B_T}-$, and let $V_T$ restrict $S_T$-modules to $B_T$-modules. By the localization presentation in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], $S_T=\varinjlim(B_T\xrightarrow{\varpi}B_T\to\cdots)$. Tensor commutation in [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor] gives, for any module sheaf $M$, $S_T\otimes_{B_T}M=\varinjlim(M\xrightarrow{\varpi}M\to\cdots)$. That node also states exactness of filtered colimits. Applying it to a short exact sequence shows that $S_T$ is flat over $B_T$. Consequently $C_T$ is computed termwise, and $H^q(C_TN)=\varinjlim(H^qN\xrightarrow{\varpi}H^qN\to\cdots)$. The stage-$n$ map $j_{T,n}:N\to V_TC_TN$ sends $x$ to $x/\varpi^n$; $j_{T,n+1}\varpi=j_{T,n}$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), localization; exact filtered colimits and tensor commutation (Stacks Tags 03DB, 03EP)

proof.text: The canonical isomorphism $f^{-1}B_Y\cong B_X$ is [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], applied to the finite rings $A/\varpi^n$. Inverse image, being a left adjoint, preserves the localization colimit, so $f^{-1}S_Y\cong S_X$ as well, compatibly with $B\to S$. Put $P_B=Lf_B^*$, $R_B=Rf_*^B$, $P_S=Lf_S^*$, $R_S=Rf_*^E$. Their ordinary adjunctions are [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The commuting coefficient square satisfies all hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. It supplies $d:V_YR_S\xrightarrow{\sim}R_BV_X$, the restriction/pullback comparison $b:V_XP_S\xrightarrow{\sim}P_BV_Y$, and compatibility of these comparisons with adjuncts; $V_T$ reflects isomorphisms.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, ordinary ringed operations; canonical coefficient-restriction comparison

proof.text:
Give $C_T\dashv V_T$ its normalized coefficient adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], with unit $u_T:N\to V_TC_TN$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1=j_{T,0}(x)$. Define $\beta_K:C_YR_BK\to R_SC_XK$ to be the coefficient adjunct of
$$R_BK\xrightarrow{R_Bu_{X,K}}R_BV_XC_XK\xrightarrow{d^{-1}}V_YR_SC_XK.$$
This is the canonical localization projection: the coefficient adjunct extends the displayed map by $s\otimes x\mapsto s\,x$, and $d$ is the canonical comparison of the two factorizations of direct image. In particular
$$d\,V_Y(\beta_K)j_{Y,n}=R_B(j_{X,n}).$$
For $n=0$ this is the defining coefficient-adjunction equation. For general $n$ it follows by multiplying that equation by $\varpi^{-n}$; the action on both localized targets is through the same coefficient map. All maps used here are natural in $K$.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; coefficient-adjunction normalization from Stacks Tag 07A6

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], $K$ is bounded as an ambient $B_X$-complex, so choose a representative zero below some $a$ (standard truncation). Apply [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image] to its sequence $K\xrightarrow{\varpi}K\to\cdots$. Its ring sheaf is $B_X$; every complex has the same lower bound $a$, and step 4 established qcqs. It gives
$$\varinjlim_nH^q(R_BK)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q\bigl(R_B(\varinjlim_nK)\bigr)$$
for every $q$, with the repeated-$\varpi$ transitions. Step 5 identifies the source with $H^q(V_YC_YR_BK)$ and the target with $H^q(R_BV_XC_XK)$. By the stage equation of step 7 this is exactly $H^q(d\,V_Y\beta_K)$, rather than an unspecified isomorphism. Hence $V_Y\beta_K$, and therefore $\beta_K$, is an isomorphism. No assertion that a localized $B_X$-injective is $f_*^E$-acyclic is used.

source.place: Higher direct images commute with uniformly bounded-below filtered colimits, applied to repeated multiplication by the uniformizer

proof.text: Step 3 makes $R_B$ an exact integral constructible functor, so [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] gives its raw rationalization $Rf_*^{\mathrm{rat}}$. On an integral representative $Q_XK$ take the comparison to be $\beta_K$ from steps 7--8. The formula for $J_T$ in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] identifies its source with $J_YRf_*^{\mathrm{rat}}(Q_XK)$ and its target with $Rf_*^EJ_X(Q_XK)$. Naturality extends to a rational morphism $v/\varpi^n$ by multiplying the integral naturality equation by $\varpi^{-n}$; changing a fraction representative does not change its value because $\varpi$ is invertible on the ambient $S$-modules. Thus these components define the required natural isomorphism on the whole raw rational category.

[lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction] gives completed pullback left adjoint to direct image for complete constant $A$-coefficients, with Hom bijection: precompose with the completion unit, then the ordinary adjunction. Transport it through [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. By [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] the transported left functor is the completed $B$-pullback $\widehat P_B$, and its comparison $q_M:P_BM\to\widehat P_BM$ (components the finite quotient maps) is, after restriction, the constant completion unit. [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] identifies the right functor with $R_B$ (its auxiliary prime $p\ne\ell$ is arbitrary; no characteristic hypothesis on the schemes). Thus $\widehat P_B\dashv R_B$ on complete objects. For constructible $M$, $P_BM$ is complete constructible by [lem-tw-ordinary-completed-integral-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], so $q_M$ is invertible. To compare Hom bijections, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] to $\underline A_T\to B_T$; both inverse-image identifications are isomorphisms ([lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]). Its $d$ compares the same two ringed-topos factorizations as $U_YF_R\cong F_AU_X$, and its $b^{-1}$ is the scalar-extension comparison of the constant-completion lemma. Its adjunct equation and full faithfulness of restriction on complete objects give the normalized completed bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(\widehat P_BM,K)\xrightarrow{-\circ q_M}\operatorname{Hom}(P_BM,K)\xrightarrow{h_B}\operatorname{Hom}(M,R_BK).$$
Consequently its counit $\widehat\varepsilon_K$ obeys $\widehat\varepsilon_Kq_{R_BK}=\varepsilon^B_K$, and its unit is $R_B(q_M)\eta^B_M$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, adjunction; Lemma 6.5.9; unit-compatible constant/completed coefficient transport

proof.text:
Let $c:P_SC_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}C_XP_B$ be the balanced-tensor pullback comparison, with the derived comparisons normalized by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Prove the mate equation explicitly. For $v:P_BM\to K$, put $t=C_X(v)c_M$. The normalized coefficient unit and tensor balancing give
$$V_X(t)\,b_{C_YM}^{-1}P_B(u_{Y,M})=u_{X,K}v.$$
Both sides send a representative $x$ to $v(x)\otimes1$; this equality is preserved by the canonical derived comparisons. By the adjunct compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], if $t^\sharp:C_YM\to R_SC_XK$ is its $S$-adjunct, the $B$-adjunct of the left side is $d\,V_Y(t^\sharp)u_{Y,M}$. The adjunct of the right side is $R_B(u_{X,K})h_B(v)$. The defining equation for $\beta_K$ in step 7 and naturality of $u_Y$ now imply, by the coefficient-adjunction bijection,
$$h_S(C_X(v)c_M)=\beta_K C_Y(h_B(v)).$$
This proves that the specified localization projection is the mate of the specified ordinary pullback comparison, using actual maps.

On constructible objects put $\widehat c_M=C_X(q_M)c_M:P_SC_YM\to C_X\widehat P_BM$. This is the pullback comparison in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], whose completed pullback is that of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]: both are the balanced coefficient map followed by the comparison $q_M$ of that definition, whose components are the finite quotient maps and which is invertible on constructible objects (step 10). If $w:\widehat P_BM\to K$, apply step 11 with $v=wq_M$. Step 10 identifies $h_B(wq_M)$ with the completed adjunct $\widehat h_B(w)$. Hence
$$h_S(C_X(w)\widehat c_M)=\beta_K C_Y(\widehat h_B(w)).$$
For $w=1_{\widehat P_BM}$ this gives the unit equation
$$\beta_{\widehat P_BM}C_Y(\widehat\eta_M)=R_S(\widehat c_M)\eta^S_{C_YM}.$$
For $w=\widehat\varepsilon_K$, its completed adjunct is $1_{R_BK}$, giving the counit equation
$$\varepsilon^S_{C_XK}P_S(\beta_K)=C_X(\widehat\varepsilon_K)\widehat c_{R_BK}.$$
The second equality is the transpose formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Thus the comparison identifies the specified integral adjunction maps after realization.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2 and Remark 6.8.15; explicit unit and counit identities

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] to $\widehat P_B\dashv R_B$ on the full integral constructible categories, with the raw scalar localizations $Q_T$. Each $Q_T$ is a localization in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] at $W_T=\{\varpi^n1_K\}$: it is the identity on objects and inverts $\varpi$. A functor $G$ inverting $W_T$ factors uniquely by $G'(v/\varpi^n)=G(\varpi1_K)^{-n}G(v)$. This is well defined because $\operatorname{Hom}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ is the colimit of $\operatorname{Hom}$ along $\varpi$. Natural transformations extend with the same components, so $G\mapsto G'$ is an equivalence. Preservation of these categories is step 3 for $R_B$ and [lem-tw-ordinary-completed-integral-pullback] for pullback. The supplied functor extensions are [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. The cited adjunction-localization theorem identifies the rational unit and counit with the images of the integral unit and counit, under the functor comparisons. Applying $J$ and using the two equations in step 12 proves precisely the claimed identification with the ambient $S$-module adjunction. This uses the actual localized adjunction, rather than choosing an adjunction after obtaining a functor isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15; localization of the normalized adjunction

proof.text: For a finite extension $E\subset L$, [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] supplies the coherent integral coefficient comparisons for completed pullback and ordinary direct image. Under realization, coefficient and pullback comparisons are the balanced tensor maps and associators of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization]. Step 11 identifies $\beta$ with their direct-image mate. The integral direct-image comparison for $B_E\to B_L$ and the ambient one for $E_E\to E_L$ are the canonical ring-change projection maps. The construction of step 7 and the calculation of step 11, applied to these ring maps instead of $B\to S$ [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], identify each with the mate of its balanced pullback comparison. The coefficient-pasting identity in [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1) says that the mate of the composite coefficient/pullback square is the composite of its two mates. Apply it to the two factorizations of $B_E\to E_L$, through $B_L$ and through $E_E$: after the given scalar comparisons, both left squares are the same balanced tensor reassociation. Their right mates therefore agree. This is the finite-extension compatibility square for $\beta$, including successive extensions and associators. The same equality passes to raw rationalizations by the fraction formula of step 9 and [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport].

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15; coefficient-pasting identity for the canonical mates

proof.text: When $f$ is an identity morphism, the finite-level direct-image functors and the ambient right-derived direct image are identities, and every comparison map is the identity by the normalization of the tower projections and tensor associators. The construction uses continuous $E_T$-modules throughout; no step identifies these with discrete non-torsion coefficients on the small étale site.
